learning-h3:
VALIDATED — ~8% operational inconsistency; model non-determinism is 6–7%, environment adds the rest.

NOTE: Earlier local-vs-prod comparison was invalid (different infra). This learning is based on engg's re-run in the production environment only.

Production Parity (Prod original vs Prod re-run):
  Sari:    CX 86.66% parity (13.3% inconsistent) | OBD 92.63% (7.4% inconsistent)
  Sandal:  CX 90.58% parity (9.4% inconsistent)  | OBD 97.14% (2.9% inconsistent)

  → Avg CX inconsistency:  ~11%
  → Avg OBD inconsistency: ~5%
  → Blended operational inconsistency: ~8%

Inter-Run Analysis (re-run vs re-run, same prod env):
  → ~6–7% inconsistency between identical re-runs
  → This is the floor — pure model non-determinism with temperature=0

Breakdown of the ~8% total:
  • ~6–7% = model's own stochastic behaviour (even with fixed seed/temp, inference stack introduces variance)
  • ~1–5% additional on CX = environment delta (image pipeline versioning, prompt drift, infra differences)
  • OBD is tighter (5%) because OBD images are more consistently available and less ambiguous

What this means:
  → ~1 in 12 adjudication decisions will flip if you re-run the same return
  → CX image agents are 2× more unstable than OBD — likely driven by lower CX image quality
  → Non-determinism cannot be solved by re-running (adds cost, not accuracy)

─────────────────────────────────────
Prompt Quality Observations (root cause)
─────────────────────────────────────

The instability is not just stochastic — it is structurally amplified by prompt design:

1. TOO MANY CLASSES (8 output classes)
   Current: No Issue | Misshipment | Major Damage | Minor Damage | Multiple Issue |
            Minor Missing | Major Missing | Can't Say
   Problem: Minor Damage, Multiple Issue, Minor Missing, Can't Say — these boundary
            classes have <40% inter-run consistency. The model is genuinely uncertain
            between them, and the prompt does not give it enough signal to be decisive.
   Fix: Collapse to binary (Issue / No Issue) per attribute. E.g.:
        damage_present Y/N, misshipment Y/N, missing_items Y/N, image_sufficient Y/N
        → Cleaner task, lower ambiguity, better calibrated confidence

2. BLOATED PROMPTS (~15K tokens per image agent call)
   Problem: Long prompts with dense instructions reduce the model's focus on the
            visual signal. The evaluation rubric buried in text competes with image
            understanding for attention.
   Fix: Trim to the minimum instruction set needed for binary decisions.
        Current prompt defines scoring systems, visibility tiers, confidence brackets,
        multi-scenario handling — most of this adds verbosity, not accuracy.

3. "CAN'T SAY" IS UNDER-SPECIFIED
   199 out of 390 mismatches (51%) are "Can't Say → No Issue" flips
   Problem: The current prompt's "Can't Say" criteria are too loose — model oscillates
            between "I'm uncertain" and "nothing looks wrong" on the same image.
   Fix: Define explicit Can't Say criteria (e.g., <50% image area visible, 0 wild
        images available) — turn it into a rules-based filter, not an LLM output class.

4. MAJOR/MINOR DAMAGE SPLIT IS NOISE
   Major Damage consistency: 0% | Minor Damage: 16.7%
   The Major/Minor damage distinction is the most unstable decision boundary.
   A single image flip between Major and Minor has no business impact (both → human review),
   so this distinction adds classification variance with zero adjudication value.
   Fix: Merge into single "Damage Present Y/N" binary.
learning-h6:
VALIDATED — Model upgrades do not improve accuracy; the ceiling is set by label quality.

Setup: 787 incidents × 2 agents (CX + OBD) run against Gemini 2.5 Flash (baseline), 3.0 Flash Preview, and 3.1 Pro Preview. Measured both (a) agreement with 2.5 Flash baseline and (b) accuracy vs human labels.

Agreement with 2.5 Flash baseline:
  Gemini 3.0 Flash Preview:  77.2% (CX: 73.4%, OBD: 76.5%)  ← closest to current prod
  Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview:    72.3% (CX: 73.6%, OBD: 70.9%)  ← most divergent

Human-label accuracy (the critical metric):
  Gemini 2.5 Flash:       60.3%
  Gemini 3.0 Flash Preview: 60.3%
  Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview:   60.4%
  → Virtually identical. Upgrading models gives ZERO accuracy improvement.

Key Conclusion: The hard ceiling is human label quality, not model capability (see H4). All three models agree with human labels at the same rate (~60%), meaning the ~40% disagreement is driven by labelling inconsistency — not model weakness.

Practical Implications:
1. Do NOT upgrade to 3.1 Pro — it costs more, runs slower, diverges more from current prod, and gives no accuracy lift
2. 3.0 Flash Preview is a safe migration path (lowest divergence from 2.5 Flash) when 2.5 Flash is deprecated, but expect no accuracy change
3. Before any model experiments, fix ground truth first — label quality improvement will unlock gains that model upgrades cannot
4. Shadow-mode A/B (Maglev action) remains valid for migration safety, but accuracy benchmarking should wait for a cleaned golden eval set

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
ADDENDUM — Gemini 3.1 Pro WITH Thinking (thinkingBudget=2048)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Setup: Same 787 incidents x 2 agents, re-run with thinkingBudget=2048, maxOutputTokens=1000.
Avg thinking tokens used: 498 per call (Genvoy uses thinking internally, does not surface trace in response).
Duration: 72.8 min (vs ~12 min without thinking — 6x slower).

Results:
  Overall accuracy:  59.8%  (941/1573)
  CX accuracy:       72.8%  (572/786)
  OBD accuracy:      46.9%  (369/787)
  Errors/timeouts:   1

Comparison vs 3.1 Pro without thinking:
  Overall:  59.8% vs 60.4%  → -0.6pp  (no improvement)
  CX:       72.8% vs ~73.6% → -0.8pp  (marginal regression)
  OBD:      46.9% vs ~47.2% → -0.3pp  (no change)

CONCLUSION: Thinking mode provides ZERO accuracy improvement on this task.
The model spends ~498 tokens reasoning per call but arrives at the same answers.
This further confirms that the accuracy ceiling is set by label quality (H4), not by model reasoning depth.
Enabling thinking adds 6x latency and cost with no return — do NOT enable for production adjudication.
learning-h4:
VALIDATED — Data patterns have shifted significantly from labelling data; ground truth is structurally misaligned with production distribution.

Setup: 787 Sari Misshipment incidents analysed across three image types — Catalog, OBD, and CX. Accuracy measured as predicted_class == human_label (not workflow is_accepted flag, which includes business overrides).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
CATALOG IMAGES — Sub-hypothesis 1 (New Entities)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Accuracy: 88.7% | Coverage: 100% (all incidents have catalog images)

Findings:
• Label distribution is clean and mostly binary — No Issue vs Misshipment, minimal edge-case classes
• No new entity problem: catalog images reflect the same product categories as labelling data
• Prediction distribution closely mirrors label distribution — model is well-calibrated on this signal
• Per-class: Misshipment class has slightly lower recall (~82%) vs No Issue (~92%), but both are strong
• Catalog is the most reliable signal in the pipeline for Sari Misshipment

Conclusion: H4 Sub-1 NOT validated for Catalog. No evidence of new entities or ambiguity gaps. Catalog is the gold-standard signal.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
OBD IMAGES — Sub-hypothesis 2 (Ambiguity) + Sub-hypothesis 3 (Temporal Drift)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Accuracy: 45.9% overall | With OBD image: 69.5% | Without OBD image: ~22.5%
Missing images: ~50% of incidents have no OBD image (delivery agent did not capture)
Can't Say rate: 22.3% on OBD vs 0.1% on Catalog

Findings:
• 50% OBD image coverage is the single largest driver of accuracy collapse — 47pp gap between having vs not having the image
• When image is missing, model defaults to Can't Say or No Issue, creating systematic under-prediction of Misshipment
• Can't Say (22.3%) is structurally different from labelling data — labelling was done on clear-evidence cases; production has genuinely ambiguous deliveries
• Sub-reason breakdown shows variance: partial OBD photo and multi-item-in-frame correlate with higher error rates

Conclusion: H4 Sub-2 VALIDATED for OBD. Production has significantly more ambiguous cases than labelling data. OBD is an unreliable signal without image availability gating. Fix: route to Human Review (not Reject) when OBD image is missing, not a model call.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
CX IMAGES — Sub-hypothesis 1 (New Entities) + Sub-hypothesis 3 (Temporal Drift)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Accuracy: 77.8% | Coverage: ~95% have at least 1 CX image

Findings:
• 4 unexpected label classes in production CX data NOT represented in labelling data:
  — Multiple Issue, Minor Missing, Major Missing, Mixed/multi-item photos
• These new entity classes have near-zero precision/recall because the model was never evaluated on them
• Image count variance: production has 1 to 5+ CX images per case; labelling was more standardised (mostly single-image)
• Cases with 3+ CX photos show better accuracy (74%) vs single-image cases (63%), but labelling skewed toward single-image
• Temporal drift: recent CX images show higher proportion of bundle/multi-item returns vs labelling baseline

Conclusion: H4 Sub-1 VALIDATED for CX. New entity classes (4 categories absent from labelling) cause systematic prediction failures. Fix: Re-label 500-1K production cases covering these new classes; add to the golden eval set.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
OVERALL CONCLUSION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
H4 is VALIDATED. The labelling dataset is NOT representative of production in two critical ways:
1. OBD: Production has ~50% missing images; labelling was done on cases with evidence available → ambiguity gap
2. CX: Production has new label entity classes not covered by labelling → new entity gap

This is the primary explanation for the ~60% accuracy ceiling seen in H6. Fixing data quality before re-running model experiments is the right priority order.

Action Items:
• Add OBD image availability as a conditional gate — skip OBD agent call if no image, route to Human Review
• Extend labelling to cover the 4 missing CX entity classes (est. ~2K incremental labels)
• Re-weight the golden eval set to match production distribution (50% OBD-imageless cases, new entity classes)
learning-h2:
VALIDATED — Different verticals show meaningfully different cohort sensitivity; PG and Prod diverge systematically, and the direction differs by agent.

Setup: 2,104 Sari Misshipment incidents across 5 verticals (April 1–8). Compared OBD and CX decision outputs between Production prompt (obd_decision_prod / cx_decision_prod) and PG prompt (obd_decision_pg / cx_decision_pg).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
OVERALL AGREEMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  OBD Agent: 85.9% agreement (297 divergences)
  CX Agent:  89.4% agreement (223 divergences)

Both agents are ~85–90% consistent between Prod and PG, meaning ~10–15% of adjudication decisions flip when the prompt changes.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
DIVERGENCE DIRECTION — OBD vs CX DISAGREE ON DIRECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
OBD: PG is MORE aggressive on Misshipment
  → PG upgrades 115 incidents TO Misshipment vs Prod
  → PG downgrades 79 incidents FROM Misshipment vs Prod
  → Net: +36 more Misshipments in PG vs Prod

CX: PG is LESS aggressive on Misshipment
  → PG downgrades 103 incidents FROM Misshipment vs Prod
  → PG upgrades 68 incidents TO Misshipment vs Prod
  → Net: -35 fewer Misshipments in PG vs Prod

These two effects partially cancel at the final decision level, but they indicate the PG prompt is pulling the two agents in opposite directions — OBD becomes stricter while CX becomes more lenient.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
PER VERTICAL — COHORT SENSITIVITY CONFIRMED
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Highest divergence (most sensitive cohorts):
  ethnic_set: OBD 79.4% agree, CX 85.8% agree  ← worst OBD
  cases_covers: CX 84.8% agree                  ← worst CX
  sari: OBD 84.0%, CX 90.4%

Lowest divergence (most stable cohorts):
  shirt: OBD 96.0%, CX 96.0%   ← most stable by far
  jean: OBD 89.6%, CX 90.7%

ethnic_set and sari are the most impacted verticals in both agents. These verticals likely have more visually similar product-to-return pairs (e.g., similar fabrics, bundled items) making them inherently harder and more sensitive to prompt phrasing changes.

TOP FLIP PATTERNS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
OBD top flips:
  No Issue → Misshipment: 64    ← PG more aggressive
  Misshipment → No Issue: 43   ← PG less aggressive (smaller)
  Can't Say → No Issue: 32
  Can't Say → Misshipment: 27

CX top flips:
  Misshipment → No Issue: 52   ← PG less aggressive
  No Issue → Misshipment: 36
  Misshipment → Multiple Issue: 29  ← reclassification at boundary

The Can't Say oscillation in OBD (flipping to both No Issue and Misshipment) confirms the ambiguity gap from H4 — model is at a decision boundary for these cases and prompt phrasing determines the tiebreak.

CONCLUSION & ACTIONS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
H2 is VALIDATED. Cohort sensitivity is real and statistically significant:
  • ~10–15% of decisions flip between Prod and PG across agents
  • Direction of change differs by agent (OBD becomes stricter, CX becomes more lenient)
  • ethnic_set and sari are disproportionately affected
  • shirt is the most stable vertical — likely has clearer visual signal

Action Items:
  1. Evaluate PG prompt against ethnic_set and sari specifically before any production rollout
  2. Flag the OBD/CX directional divergence to the prompt team — the PG prompt may be pulling agents out of alignment with each other
  3. Consider vertical-specific evaluation thresholds: shirt can tolerate bolder prompt changes; ethnic_set needs conservative changes
  4. The Can't Say ambiguity pattern reinforces H4 finding — add explicit Can't Say criteria to anchor borderline OBD decisions
